- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift downward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price has recently spiked, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or adjust downward after spike.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias toward prior 5–7 day average if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If model forecast is flat or rising slowly but true price drops sharply, consider lag error — adjust forecast to reflect recent sentiment reversal or downward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is negative or mixed, avoid linear extrapolation; use weighted average of recent 7–10 day mean + sentiment-adjusted volatility buffer.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly optimistic; apply a downward bias of 1–3% to forecast unless sentiment turns positive.
